title: Invented-language test: design a constructed language and run it against every fact
statement: Design a constructed language a 15th-century author could have made: a lexicon of roots grouped by meaning (plants, stars, bathing, body), affix rules, and a script mapping into EVA glyphs. Write text in it about each illustrated section's subject, laid out like the manuscript, and send it once as attack.json {"attack": "generator", "hypothesis": "invented_language", "title", "method", "cut": "lines", "lines": [...]}. Fit nothing on the hidden pages. It earns credit only where meaningless procedures fail: a fact they miss (currently F-019), or meaning-linked predictions you register first as facts (section words follow the subject; labels share roots with the text about the same object). Reproducing what meaningless text already reproduces proves nothing; say so in the method if that is the outcome.
